assumptions: Incoming official-message obligations and the October 2026 activation catalyst remain materially relevant.
Accounting firms are permitted and willing to coordinate mailbox triage for clients.
Exception handling averages near the stated 10-20 minutes per active entity monthly.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid accountant-led pilot covering multiple entities with measured message frequency, handling time, renewal intent, security acceptance, and positive channel unit economics.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Selling accountable triage and deadline ownership rather than duplicating a free government mailbox is the correct value layer.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Missed official messages can be costly, but message frequency, existing delegation adequacy, and willingness to pay 49-149 PLN monthly are unknown.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid subscriptions, low software costs, and accountant portfolios could support favorable CAC, but human exception load and the assumed 8,000-entity scale are unvalidated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Accounting firms managing many Polish SMEs provide a focused and potentially large beachhead with shared operational pain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A multi-entity SLA layer may win accountant portfolios, but public delegation tools and accounting suites can absorb basic alerting and workflow features.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The service can extend into other official channels, document workflows, compliance calendars, and multi-entity back-office operations.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Resolution playbooks and embedded accountant workflows can create switching costs, but mailbox authorization is revocable and classification technology is replicable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Accountable escalation may be meaningfully more reliable than alerts, but no proof shows that SMEs need it beyond free administrator functionality.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The October 2026 activation deadline creates a strong acquisition window, though proposed legislative changes introduce scope uncertainty.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: One accounting partnership can aggregate many entities and keep CAC low, but no signed partner or tested revenue share is supplied.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A forwarded-message pilot is inexpensive and part-time compatible, but secure access, deadline liability, integrations, and analyst coverage must be resolved before strong SLAs.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a portfolio-level accounting-firm agreement with formal mailbox authorization, standardized escalation responsibility, and minimum committed entity volume.
main_structural_strength: Accountant portfolio distribution can aggregate fragmented SMEs and turn a low-priced workflow into recurring scale.
primary_score_limiter: The free mailbox and delegation features may already solve most of the problem, leaving uncertain usage frequency and willingness to pay.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The government inbox is free and supports administrator delegation, while proposed legislative changes could narrow required usage.
